findings.title: Quick-hide branch leaves wallet-attempt review and clear controls unreachable in core routes

evidence.meaning: Optional wallet prop gates visible records and the only rendered clear control; omitted prop always yields an empty visible list.
Input branch mounts WalletAttempts with no wallet prop.
Review branch mounts WalletAttempts with no wallet prop.
Registry route mounts WalletAttempts with no wallet prop.
Payment attempt identity uses chain plus invoice scope, not the currently selected account.
beginAttempt executes before the provider submission; the returned hash updates but retains the attempt.
An existing same-key record blocks beginAttempt, with no expiry or automatic eviction; explicit clear removes it.
Connected component test manually supplies wallet; omitted-wallet test intentionally hides clear while preserving duplicate protection, leaving route wiring uncovered.

findings.reachable_flow: Core Pay and Registry mount the component without props. Once the tab journal contains an attempt, the component can display its generic warning but treats wallet as undefined regardless of the actual connection. It never renders the record, returned hash, or confirmed-clear button. A subsequent matching action is rejected by beginAttempt before a new provider submission, and the record does not expire automatically.
findings.practical_impact: Users cannot review or clear unresolved attempt records through the core route UI, so retry/recovery for a matching payment or registry action stays blocked while that record remains in the tab journal. Changing a payment account does not change the invoice-scoped duplicate key. This is a recovery/availability regression; no loss of funds is established.
findings.remediation_direction: Pass the current connected wallet context to WalletAttempts at every core caller. Make the integration contract explicit so omitted wallet wiring cannot silently compile. Add route-level coverage for pre-existing attempt review and confirmed clearing across connected, disconnected, account-change and chain-change states, while retaining privacy gating and duplicate-submission protection.
